title: Rejection implies bounded halting
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with initial label $l_0$, let an oracle answer queries to its deciders, and let $x$ be a Boolean input. For any label $l$, register assignment $v$, output word, register $r$, and integer $W\ge 0$, if the run of the compiled program from the configuration initialized by $x$, $v$, and that output rejects at register $r$ with head position reset to $0$, then it halts with output bit $0$ and all work-tape heads in the interval $[-1,W]$. Before halting, every configuration is between ordinary machine steps rather than oracle calls, and all its work-tape heads lie in $[-1,W]$.
